from datetime import datetime
from unittest import TestCase
import jwt
import pytest
from aggrep.utils import (
    decode_token,
    encode_token,
    get_cache_key,
    now,
    overlap,
    slugify,
)

class TestUtilityFunctions(TestCase):
    """Refactored utility function test suite."""
    
    def test_overlap_coefficient(self):
        """Verify overlap coefficient calculations."""
        # Identical sets should yield full overlap (1.0)
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar"}, {"foo", "bar"}) == 1
        
        # Partial overlap: one common element out of two in each set
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar"}, {"foo", "baz"}) == 0.5
        
        # Subset relationship: first set contains second completely
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar"}, {"foo", "bar", "baz"}) == 1
        
        # Single-element intersection from larger set
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar", "baz", "qux", "quux"}, {"quux"}) == 1
        
        # Completely disjoint sets
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar", "baz"}, {"qux", "quux"}) == 0
        
        # Empty intersection despite different sizes
        assert overlap({"foo", "bar", "baz", "qux"}, {"quux"}) == 0
    
    def test_string_normalization(self):
        """Test string transformation to URL-safe slugs."""
        # Standard phrase conversion
        assert slugify("Test Slugify function") == "test-slugify-function"
        
        # Already normalized input
        assert slugify("foobar") == "foobar"
        
        # Numeric input conversion
        assert slugify(12345) == "12345"
        
        # None value handling
        assert slugify(None) == "none"
    
    def test_jwt_token_decoding(self):
        """Validate JWT token decoding and expiration handling."""
        current_time = now().timestamp()
        
        # Valid token verification
        valid_token = encode_token("k1", "v1", "secret", time=current_time)
        assert decode_token("k1", "secret", valid_token) == "v1"
        
        # Expired token due to old timestamp
        old_token = encode_token("k2", "v2", "secret", time=current_time - 1000)
        with pytest.raises(jwt.exceptions.ExpiredSignatureError):
            decode_token("k2", "secret", old_token)
        
        # Token with explicit short expiry
        expiring_token = encode_token("k3", "v3", "secret", 
                                     time=current_time - 100, expires_in=10)
        with pytest.raises(jwt.exceptions.ExpiredSignatureError):
            decode_token("k3", "secret", expiring_token)
        
        # Invalid token format handling
        assert decode_token("k1", "secret", "iam.aninvalid.jsonwwebtoken") is None
    
    def test_jwt_token_encoding(self):
        """Confirm deterministic JWT token generation."""
        fixed_time = datetime(2019, 9, 1).timestamp()
        expected_token = "<KEY>"  # noqa
        assert encode_token("key", "value", "secret", time=fixed_time) == expected_token
    
    def test_cache_key_generation(self):
        """Ensure consistent cache key creation from parameters."""
        # Basic key construction
        base_key = get_cache_key("endpoint", "identity", 1, 10, "latest", route_arg=None)
        assert base_key == "endpoint_identity_1_10_latest"
        
        # Key with additional route argument
        extended_key = get_cache_key("endpoint", "identity", 2, 10, "popular", 
                                    route_arg="arg")
        assert extended_key == "endpoint_identity_2_10_popular_arg"
        
        # Anonymous user handling
        anon_key = get_cache_key("endpoint", None, 2, 10, "popular")
        assert anon_key == "endpoint_anonymous_2_10_popular"

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from .spectral_normalization import SpectralNorm
import logging

class Graph_GAN(nn.Module):
    """Refactored implementation of Graph GAN architecture with modularized components"""
    
    def __init__(self, generator, config):
        super(Graph_GAN, self).__init__()
        self.config = config
        self.is_generator = generator
        self.is_discriminator = not generator
        
        # Configure spectral normalization and batch norm settings
        self._setup_norm_config()
        
        # Initialize networks based on generator/discriminator role
        self._initialize_networks(generator)
        
        # Setup dropout layer
        dropout_rate = config.gen_dropout if self.is_generator else config.disc_dropout
        self.dropout_layer = nn.Dropout(p=dropout_rate)
        
        # Apply Xavier initialization if specified
        if config.glorot:
            self._xavier_initialization()
            
        # Apply spectral normalization if enabled
        if config.spectral_norm:
            self._apply_spectral_norm()
            
        # Log model configuration
        self._log_model_info()

    def _setup_norm_config(self):
        """Configure normalization parameters based on generator/discriminator"""
        cfg = self.config
        cfg.spectral_norm = (
            cfg.spectral_norm_gen if self.is_generator else cfg.spectral_norm_disc
        )
        cfg.batch_norm = cfg.batch_norm_gen if self.is_generator else cfg.batch_norm_disc
        cfg.mp_iterations = cfg.mp_iters_gen if self.is_generator else cfg.mp_iters_disc
        cfg.fe1 = cfg.fe1g if self.is_generator else cfg.fe1d
        
        # Set additional flags for generator/discriminator
        if self.is_generator:
            cfg.dea = False
        if self.is_discriminator:
            cfg.lfc = False
            
    def _initialize_networks(self, generator):
        """Initialize the main components of the GAN architecture"""
        cfg = self.config
        
        # Determine first layer node size
        self.first_layer_node_size = (
            cfg.latent_node_size if cfg.latent_node_size else cfg.hidden_node_size
        ) if generator else cfg.node_feat_size
        
        # Ensure fe1 is properly initialized
        if not cfg.fe1:
            cfg.fe1 = cfg.fe.copy()
        cfg.fn1 = cfg.fn.copy()
        
        # Calculate ancillary features for edge network
        ancillary_features = self._calculate_ancillary_features(cfg)
        
        # Setup LFC layer if needed
        if cfg.lfc:
            self.lfc = nn.Linear(
                cfg.lfc_latent_size, cfg.num_hits * self.first_layer_node_size
            )
            
        # Build message passing networks
        self._build_message_passing_networks(ancillary_features)
        
        # Build discriminator-specific components
        if self.is_discriminator and cfg.dea:
            self._build_discriminator_head(cfg)
            
        # Build generator mask learning components
        if self.is_generator and (cfg.mask_learn or cfg.mask_learn_sep):
            self._build_mask_learning_components(cfg)

    def _calculate_ancillary_features(self, cfg):
        """Calculate number of ancillary features for edge network"""
        anc = 0
        if cfg.pos_diffs:
            if cfg.deltacoords:
                if cfg.coords == "cartesian":
                    anc += 3
                elif cfg.coords in ["polar", "polarrel"]:
                    anc += 2
            if cfg.deltar:
                anc += 1
        anc += int(cfg.int_diffs)
        return anc

    def _build_message_passing_networks(self, anc):
        """Build the core message passing neural networks"""
        cfg = self.config
        self.message_passing_layers = cfg.mp_iterations
        
        # Initialize network containers
        self.edge_nets = nn.ModuleList()
        self.node_nets = nn.ModuleList()
        self.edge_batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        self.node_batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        
        # Build first MP layer
        self._build_first_mp_layer(anc)
        
        # Build remaining MP layers
        for _ in range(cfg.mp_iterations - 1):
            self._build_additional_mp_layer(anc)

    def _build_first_mp_layer(self, anc):
        """Build the first message passing layer"""
        cfg = self.config
        
        # Edge network setup for first layer
        fe_in_size = (
            2 * self.first_layer_node_size
            + anc
            + cfg.clabels_first_layer
            + cfg.mask_fne_np
        )
        fe_params = [fe_in_size] + cfg.fe1
        self._build_edge_network(fe_params)
        
        # Node network setup for first layer
        fn_out_size = cfg.fe1[-1]
        fn_in_size = (
            fn_out_size
            + self.first_layer_node_size
            + cfg.clabels_first_layer
            + cfg.mask_fne_np
        )
        fn_params = [fn_in_size] + cfg.fn1 + [cfg.hidden_node_size]
        self._build_node_network(fn_params)

    def _build_additional_mp_layer(self, anc):
        """Build additional message passing layers"""
        cfg = self.config
        
        # Edge network setup for subsequent layers
        fe_in_size = (
            2 * cfg.hidden_node_size
            + anc
            + cfg.clabels_hidden_layers
            + cfg.mask_fne_np
        )
        fe_params = [fe_in_size] + cfg.fe
        self._build_edge_network(fe_params)
        
        # Node network setup for subsequent layers
        fn_out_size = cfg.fe[-1]
        fn_in_size = (
            fn_out_size
            + cfg.hidden_node_size
            + cfg.clabels_hidden_layers
            + cfg.mask_fne_np
        )
        fn_params = [fn_in_size] + cfg.fn + [cfg.hidden_node_size]
        self._build_node_network(fn_params)

    def _build_edge_network(self, params):
        """Build an edge network from parameter list"""
        cfg = self.config
        edge_net = nn.ModuleList()
        batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        
        for i in range(len(params) - 1):
            linear = nn.Linear(params[i], params[i + 1])
            edge_net.append(linear)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                batch_norms.append(nn.BatchNorm1d(params[i + 1]))
                
        self.edge_nets.append(edge_net)
        if cfg.batch_norm:
            self.edge_batch_norms.append(batch_norms)

    def _build_node_network(self, params):
        """Build a node network from parameter list"""
        cfg = self.config
        node_net = nn.ModuleList()
        batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        
        for i in range(len(params) - 1):
            linear = nn.Linear(params[i], params[i + 1])
            node_net.append(linear)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                batch_norms.append(nn.BatchNorm1d(params[i + 1]))
                
        self.node_nets.append(node_net)
        if cfg.batch_norm:
            self.node_batch_norms.append(batch_norms)

    def _build_discriminator_head(self, cfg):
        """Build discriminator head network"""
        fnd_params = [cfg.hidden_node_size + int(cfg.mask_fnd_np)] + cfg.fnd + [1]
        self.disc_head = nn.ModuleList()
        self.disc_batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        
        for i in range(len(fnd_params) - 1):
            linear = nn.Linear(fnd_params[i], fnd_params[i + 1])
            self.disc_head.append(linear)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                self.disc_batch_norms.append(nn.BatchNorm1d(fnd_params[i + 1]))

    def _build_mask_learning_components(self, cfg):
        """Build mask learning components for generator"""
        fmg_params = [self.first_layer_node_size] + cfg.fmg
        if cfg.mask_learn:
            fmg_params.append(1)
        else:
            fmg_params.append(cfg.num_hits)
            
        self.mask_generators = nn.ModuleList()
        self.mask_batch_norms = nn.ModuleList() if cfg.batch_norm else None
        
        for i in range(len(fmg_params) - 1):
            linear = nn.Linear(fmg_params[i], fmg_params[i + 1])
            self.mask_generators.append(linear)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                self.mask_batch_norms.append(nn.BatchNorm1d(fmg_params[i + 1]))

    def _xavier_initialization(self):
        """Apply Xavier uniform initialization to all linear layers"""
        for module in self.modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                torch.nn.init.xavier_uniform_(module.weight, gain=self.config.glorot)

    def _apply_spectral_norm(self):
        """Apply spectral normalization to all applicable layers"""
        # Apply to edge networks
        for edge_net in self.edge_nets:
            for layer in edge_net:
                if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
                    layer = SpectralNorm(layer)
                    
        # Apply to node networks
        for node_net in self.node_nets:
            for layer in node_net:
                if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
                    layer = SpectralNorm(layer)
                    
        # Apply to discriminator head if exists
        if hasattr(self, 'disc_head'):
            for layer in self.disc_head:
                if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
                    layer = SpectralNorm(layer)
                    
        # Apply to mask generators if exists
        if hasattr(self, 'mask_generators'):
            for layer in self.mask_generators:
                if isinstance(layer, nn.Linear):
                    layer = SpectralNorm(layer)

    def _log_model_info(self):
        """Log model configuration information"""
        if hasattr(self, 'lfc'):
            logging.info("LFC: ")
            logging.info(self.lfc)
            
        logging.info("Edge Networks: ")
        logging.info(self.edge_nets)
        logging.info("Node Networks: ")
        logging.info(self.node_nets)
        
        if hasattr(self, 'disc_head'):
            logging.info("Discriminator Head: ")
            logging.info(self.disc_head)
            
        if hasattr(self, 'mask_generators'):
            logging.info("Mask Generators: ")
            logging.info(self.mask_generators)

    def forward(self, x, labels=None, epoch=0):
        batch_size = x.shape[0]
        logging.debug(f"Input x: {x}")
        
        # Apply LFC if configured
        if hasattr(self, 'lfc'):
            x = self.lfc(x).reshape(batch_size, self.config.num_hits, self.first_layer_node_size)
            logging.debug(f"After LFC: {x}")
            
        # Handle masking logic
        mask = self._process_mask(x, labels, epoch)
        
        # Message passing iterations
        for i in range(self.message_passing_layers):
            x = self._message_passing_iteration(x, i, batch_size, mask, labels)
            
        # Final output processing
        return self._process_output(x, mask)

    def _process_mask(self, x, labels, epoch):
        """Process masking logic for generator/discriminator"""
        try:
            # Determine if masking should be applied
            mask_required = (
                (self.is_discriminator and (
                    self.config.mask_manual or 
                    self.config.mask_real_only or 
                    self.config.mask_learn or 
                    self.config.mask_c or 
                    self.config.mask_learn_sep
                )) or
                (self.is_generator and (
                    self.config.mask_learn or 
                    self.config.mask_c or 
                    self.config.mask_learn_sep
                )) and epoch >= self.config.mask_epoch
            )
            
            # Extract mask from input if needed
            if self.is_discriminator and (mask_required or self.config.mask_fnd_np):
                mask = x[:, :, 3:4] + 0.5
                
            # Process different masking modes
            if self.is_discriminator and (
                self.config.mask_manual or 
                self.config.mask_learn or 
                self.config.mask_c or 
                self.config.mask_learn_sep
            ):
                x = x[:, :, :3]
                
            # Generator mask learning
            if self.is_generator and self.config.mask_learn:
                mask = self._generate_mask(x, self.mask_generators, self.mask_batch_norms)
                
            # Generator conditional masking
            if self.is_generator and self.config.mask_c:
                nump = (labels[:, self.config.clabels] * self.config.num_hits).int() - 1
                mask = (x[:, :, 0].argsort(1).argsort(1) <= nump.unsqueeze(1)).unsqueeze(2).float()
                
            # Handle num particles for masking
            if self.config.mask_fne_np:
                nump = torch.mean(mask, dim=1)
                
            # Generator separate mask learning
            if self.is_generator and self.config.mask_learn_sep:
                nump = x[:, -1, :]
                x = x[:, :-1, :]
                nump = self._generate_mask(nump, self.mask_generators, self.mask_batch_norms)
                nump = torch.argmax(nump, dim=1)
                mask = (x[:, :, 0].argsort(1).argsort(1) <= nump.unsqueeze(1)).unsqueeze(2).float()
                
            return mask if mask_required else None
            
        except AttributeError:
            return None

    def _generate_mask(self, x, modules, batch_norms):
        """Generate mask using MLP"""
        mask = F.leaky_relu(modules[0](x), negative_slope=self.config.leaky_relu_alpha)
        if batch_norms:
            mask = batch_norms[0](mask)
        mask = self.dropout_layer(mask)
        
        for i in range(1, len(modules)):
            mask = F.leaky_relu(
                modules[i](mask), negative_slope=self.config.leaky_relu_alpha
            )
            if batch_norms:
                mask = batch_norms[i-1](mask)
            mask = self.dropout_layer(mask)
            
        return torch.sign(mask) if self.config.mask_learn_bin else torch.sigmoid(mask)

    def _message_passing_iteration(self, x, layer_idx, batch_size, mask, labels):
        """Perform one iteration of message passing"""
        cfg = self.config
        
        # Get layer-specific parameters
        clabel_iter = cfg.clabels and (
            (layer_idx == 0 and cfg.clabels_first_layer) or
            (layer_idx and cfg.clabels_hidden_layers)
        )
        
        # Prepare adjacency matrix
        A, A_mask = self._compute_adjacency(x, layer_idx, batch_size, mask)
        
        # Process through edge network
        for j in range(len(self.edge_nets[layer_idx])):
            A = F.leaky_relu(self.edge_nets[layer_idx][j](A), negative_slope=cfg.leaky_relu_alpha)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                A = self.edge_batch_norms[layer_idx][j](A)
            A = self.dropout_layer(A)
            
        # Aggregate messages
        A = A.view(batch_size, cfg.num_hits, cfg.num_knn, -1)
        if mask is not None:
            if cfg.fully_connected:
                A = A * mask.unsqueeze(1)
            else:
                A = A * A_mask.reshape(batch_size, cfg.num_hits, cfg.num_knn, 1)
                
        A = torch.sum(A, 2) if cfg.sum else torch.mean(A, 2)
        
        # Concatenate with original features
        x = torch.cat((A, x), 2).view(batch_size * cfg.num_hits, -1)
        
        # Process through node network
        for j in range(len(self.node_nets[layer_idx]) - 1):
            x = F.leaky_relu(self.node_nets[layer_idx][j](x), negative_slope=cfg.leaky_relu_alpha)
            if cfg.batch_norm:
                x = self.node_batch_norms[layer_idx][j](x)
            x = self.dropout_layer(x)
            
        x = self.dropout_layer(self.node_nets[layer_idx][-1](x))
        x = x.view(batch_size, cfg.num_hits, cfg.hidden_node_size)
        
        return x

    def _compute_adjacency(self, x, layer_idx, batch_size, mask):
        """Compute adjacency matrix for message passing"""
        cfg = self.config
        node_size = x.size(2)
        num_coords = 3 if cfg.coords == "cartesian" else 2
        
        if cfg.fully_connected:
            # Fully connected graph construction
            x1 = x.repeat(1, 1, cfg.num_hits).view(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_hits, node_size
            )
            x2 = x.repeat(1, cfg.num_hits, 1)
            
            if cfg.pos_diffs:
                if cfg.all_ef and not (self.is_discriminator and layer_idx == 0):
                    diffs = x2 - x1
                else:
                    diffs = x2[:, :, :num_coords] - x1[:, :, :num_coords]
                    
                dists = torch.norm(diffs + 1e-12, dim=2).unsqueeze(2)
                
                if cfg.deltar and cfg.deltacoords:
                    A = torch.cat((x1, x2, diffs, dists), 2)
                elif cfg.deltar:
                    A = torch.cat((x1, x2, dists), 2)
                elif cfg.deltacoords:
                    A = torch.cat((x1, x2, diffs), 2)
                A = A.view(batch_size * cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_hits, -1)
            else:
                A = torch.cat((x1, x2), 2).view(
                    batch_size * cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_hits, -1
                )
        else:
            # K-nearest neighbors graph construction
            x1 = x.repeat(1, 1, cfg.num_hits).view(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_hits, node_size
            )
            
            if mask is not None:
                mul = 1e4
                x2 = (((1 - mul) * mask + mul) * x).repeat(1, cfg.num_hits, 1)
            else:
                x2 = x.repeat(1, cfg.num_hits, 1)
                
            if (cfg.all_ef or not cfg.pos_diffs) and not (self.is_discriminator and layer_idx == 0):
                diffs = x2 - x1
            else:
                diffs = x2[:, :, :num_coords] - x1[:, :, :num_coords]
                
            dists = torch.norm(diffs + 1e-12, dim=2).reshape(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits, cfg.num_hits
            )
            
            # Find k nearest neighbors
            sorted_dists = torch.sort(dists, dim=2)
            self_loops = 0 if cfg.self_loops else 1
            dists_knn = sorted_dists[0][:, :, self_loops:cfg.num_knn+self_loops].reshape(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_knn, 1
            )
            indices_knn = sorted_dists[1][:, :, self_loops:cfg.num_knn+self_loops].reshape(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_knn, 1
            )
            
            # Gather kNN features
            x1_knn = x.repeat(1, 1, cfg.num_knn).view(
                batch_size, cfg.num_hits * cfg.num_knn, node_size
            )
            
            if mask is not None:
                x2_knn = torch.gather(
                    torch.cat((x, mask), dim=2), 1, indices_knn.repeat(1, 1, node_size+1)
                )
                A_mask = x2_knn[:, :, -1:]
                x2_knn = x2_knn[:, :, :-1]
            else:
                x2_knn = torch.gather(x, 1, indices_knn.repeat(1, 1, node_size))
                
            if cfg.pos_diffs:
                A = torch.cat((x1_knn, x2_knn, dists_knn), dim=2)
            else:
                A = torch.cat((x1_knn, x2_knn), dim=2)
                
        return A, A_mask if mask is not None else None

    def _process_output(self, x, mask):
        """Process final output for generator or discriminator"""
        if self.is_generator:
            # Generator output processing
            x = (
                torch.tanh(x[:, :, :self.config.node_feat_size])
                if self.config.gtanh
                else x[:, :, :self.config.node_feat_size]
            )
            
            if mask is not None:
                x = torch.cat((x, mask - 0.5), dim=2)
                
            if hasattr(self.config, "mask_feat_bin") and self.config.mask_feat_bin:
                mask_binary = (x[:, :, 3:4] < 0).float() - 0.5
                x = torch.cat((x[:, :, :3], mask_binary), dim=2)
                
            return x
        else:
            # Discriminator output processing
            if self.config.dea:
                if mask is not None:
                    x = x * mask
                    x = torch.sum(x, 1)
                    if not self.config.sum:
                        x = x / (torch.sum(mask, 1) + 1e-12)
                else:
                    x = torch.sum(x, 1) if self.config.sum else torch.mean(x, 1)
                    
                if hasattr(self.config, "mask_fnd_np") and self.config.mask_fnd_np:
                    num_particles = torch.mean(mask, dim=1)
                    x = torch.cat((num_particles, x), dim=1)
                    
                for i in range(len(self.disc_head) - 1):
                    x = F.leaky_relu(self.disc_head[i](x), negative_slope=self.config.leaky_relu_alpha)
                    if self.config.batch_norm:
                        x = self.disc_batch_norms[i](x)
                    x = self.dropout_layer(x)
                    
                x = self.dropout_layer(self.disc_head[-1](x))
            else:
                x = x[:, :, :1]
                if mask is not None:
                    x = x * mask
                    x = torch.sum(x, 1) / (torch.sum(mask, 1) + 1e-12)
                else:
                    x = torch.mean(x, 1)
                    
            return x if (self.config.loss == "w" or self.config.loss == "hinge") else torch.sigmoid(x)

    def load_weights(self, checkpoint):
        """Load weights from a checkpoint"""
        for m_from, m_to in zip(checkpoint.modules(), self.modules()):
            if isinstance(m_to, nn.Linear):
                m_to.weight.data = m_from.weight.data.clone()
                if m_to.bias is not None:
                    m_to.bias.data = m_from.bias.data.clone()

    def reset_weights(self):
        """Reset all linear layer parameters"""
        for module in self.modules():
            if isinstance(module, nn.Linear):
                module.reset_parameters()

# Type III Clone: Reorganized logging initialization and handler setup logic
import os
import logging
import logging.handlers
from wok.config.data import Data

# Default configuration values
DEFAULT_LOG_FORMAT = "%(asctime)s %(name)-20s [%(levelname)-7s] %(message)s"
DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"

# Mapping of log level names to their numeric constants
LOG_LEVEL_MAP = {
    "debug": logging.DEBUG,
    "info": logging.INFO,
    "warn": logging.WARNING,
    "error": logging.ERROR,
    "critical": logging.CRITICAL,
    "notset": logging.NOTSET
}

# Global state tracking
logging_initialized = False


def setup_logging(config=None, fmt=None, date_fmt=None, level=None):
    """
    Initialize the logging infrastructure.
    
    Accepts config in multiple forms:
    - None: Use default empty configuration
    - dict-like: Create structured configuration
    - string: Treat as log level for root logger
    - list: Directly configure loggers
    
    Parameters:
        config: Configuration source (dict, str, list, or Data object)
        fmt: Custom log format string
        date_fmt: Custom date/time format
        level: Log level override
    """
    global logging_initialized
    
    # Normalize input configuration
    if config is None:
        config = Data.element()
    elif not isinstance(config, str):
        config = Data.create(config)
    
    # Determine logger configurations
    if Data.is_list(config):
        logger_configs = config
        config = Data.element()
    elif Data.is_element(config):
        logger_configs = config.get("loggers", default=Data.list)
    elif isinstance(config, str):
        logger_configs = Data.list([["", config]])
        config = Data.element()
    
    # Resolve formatting options
    effective_format = fmt or config.get("format", DEFAULT_LOG_FORMAT)
    effective_datefmt = date_fmt or config.get("datefmt", DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT)
    
    # Apply base logging configuration
    logging.basicConfig(format=effective_format, datefmt=effective_datefmt)
    
    # Process each logger configuration
    for logger_name, logger_config in logger_configs:
        configure_logger(logger_name, config=logger_config)
    
    # Apply optional global level override
    if level is not None:
        configure_logger("", conf=level)
    
    logging_initialized = True


def resolve_log_level(level_name):
    """Convert a log level name to its corresponding numeric constant."""
    return LOG_LEVEL_MAP.get(level_name.lower(), "notset")


def acquire_logger(name="", level=None, config=None):
    """
    Retrieve a configured logger instance.
    
    Args:
        name: Logger identifier (empty string for root logger)
        level: Optional log level specification
        config: Additional configuration data
        
    Returns:
        Configured logging.Logger instance
    """
    global logging_initialized
    
    if not logging_initialized:
        setup_logging(config)
    
    logger = logging.getLogger(name)
    
    # Apply additional configuration if provided
    if config is not None:
        configure_logger(logger, config)
    
    # Set explicit level if specified
    if level is not None:
        logger.setLevel(resolve_log_level(level))
    
    return logger


def configure_logger(logger_obj, config_data):
    """
    Configure a logger using structured configuration data.
    
    Supports two forms:
    - Simple string: interpreted as log level
    - Dictionary/element: contains 'level' and/or 'handlers' configuration
    
    Args:
        logger_obj: Logger instance or name string
        config_data: Configuration specification
    """
    # Convert string logger name to actual logger object
    if isinstance(logger_obj, str):
        logger_obj = acquire_logger(logger_obj)
    
    # Normalize configuration to element structure
    if isinstance(config_data, str):
        config_data = Data.element(dict(level=config_data))
    else:
        config_data = Data.create(config_data)
    
    # Apply log level if specified
    level_spec = config_data.get("level")
    if level_spec is not None:
        logger_obj.setLevel(resolve_log_level(level_spec))
    
    # Process handlers configuration
    handlers_spec = config_data.get("handlers", default=Data.list)
    if Data.is_element(handlers_spec):
        handlers_spec = Data.list([handlers_spec])
    
    for handler_config in handlers_spec:
        handler_instance = create_handler(logger_obj, handler_config)
        if handler_instance is not None:
            logger_obj.addHandler(handler_instance)


def create_handler(logger, config):
    """
    Create and configure a logging handler based on specification.
    
    Args:
        logger: Parent logger instance
        config: Handler configuration specification
        
    Returns:
        Configured handler instance or None if invalid
    """
    # Validate configuration structure
    if not Data.is_element(config):
        logger.error("Malformed log handler configuration:\n{0}".format(repr(config)))
        return None
    
    handler_type = config.get("type")
    if handler_type is None or not isinstance(handler_type, str) or handler_type.lower() not in HANDLER_REGISTRY:
        logger.error("Unknown or unsupported handler type: {0}\n{1}".format(handler_type, repr(config)))
        return None
    
    # Instantiate handler using appropriate factory
    handler = HANDLER_REGISTRY[handler_type.lower()](config)
    
    # Apply optional log level
    level_spec = config.get("level")
    if level_spec is not None:
        handler.setLevel(resolve_log_level(level_spec))
    
    # Apply formatting
    format_spec = config.get("format", DEFAULT_LOG_FORMAT)
    if format_spec is not None:
        if Data.is_list(format_spec):
            format_spec = "".join(format_spec.to_native())
        handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(format_spec))
    
    return handler


def create_smtp_handler(config):
    """Create an SMTP handler for email notifications."""
    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    # Verify required fields
    missing_fields = config.missing_keys(["host", "user", "from", "to", "subject"])
    if missing_fields:
        logger.error("Missing required SMTP handler fields: {0}\n{1}".format(", ".join(missing_fields), repr(config)))
        return None
    
    # Build mail host specification
    mail_host = config.get("host")
    port = config.get("port")
    if port is not None:
        mail_host = (mail_host, port)
    
    # Prepare authentication credentials
    username = config.get("user")
    password = config.get("pass")
    credentials = (username, password) if password is not None else username
    
    # Construct handler with all parameters
    from_addr = config.get("from")
    to_addrs = config.get("to")
    subject = config.get("subject")
    
    return logging.handlers.SMTPHandler(
        mailhost=mail_host,
        fromaddr=from_addr,
        toaddrs=to_addrs,
        subject=subject,
        credentials=credentials,
        secure=tuple()
    )


def create_file_handler(config):
    """Create a file-based logging handler."""
    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    # Check required filename parameter
    missing_fields = config.missing_keys(["filename"])
    if missing_fields:
        logger.error("Missing required file handler fields: {0}\n{1}".format(", ".join(missing_fields), repr(config)))
        return None
    
    # Ensure directory exists
    filepath = config["filename"]
    directory = os.path.dirname(filepath)
    if directory and not os.path.exists(directory):
        os.makedirs(directory)
    
    # Open file in append mode by default
    mode = config.get("mode", "a")
    return logging.FileHandler(filepath, mode)


def create_timed_rotating_file_handler(config):
    """Create a time-based rotating file handler."""
    logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    
    # Verify required parameters
    missing_fields = config.missing_keys(["filename", "when", "interval"])
    if missing_fields:
        logger.error("Missing required timed rotating file handler fields: {0}\n{1}".format(", ".join(missing_fields), repr(config)))
        return None
    
    # Ensure directory exists
    filepath = config["filename"]
    directory = os.path.dirname(filepath)
    if directory and not os.path.exists(directory):
        os.makedirs(directory)
    
    # Create handler with rotation parameters
    rotation_when = config["when"]
    rotation_interval = config["interval"]
    
    return logging.handlers.TimedRotatingFileHandler(
        filename=filepath,
        when=rotation_when,
        interval=rotation_interval
    )


# Registry mapping handler types to their creation functions
HANDLER_REGISTRY = {
    "smtp": create_smtp_handler,
    "file": create_file_handler,
    "timed_rotating_file": create_timed_rotating_file_handler
}

import logging
import time
import socket
import errno
from contextlib import contextmanager
import click

@contextmanager
def managed_socket(*args, **kwargs):
    """Context manager to create and automatically close a socket"""
    s = socket.socket(*args, **kwargs)
    try:
        yield s
    finally:
        s.close()

def await_port_open(port: int, max_wait: float = 30.0, quiet: bool = False) -> None:
    """Wait until a specified port becomes available (listening)
    
    Args:
        port (int): Target port number
        max_wait (float): Maximum waiting time in seconds (default: 30.0)
        quiet (bool): If True, suppress informational messages
        
    Raises:
        TimeoutError: Raised if the port does not open within the timeout period
    """
    start_time = time.monotonic()
    deadline = start_time + max_wait
    
    while True:
        if port_is_listening(port):
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start_time
            if not quiet:
                logging.info("Port is now listening. Duration=%.3fs", elapsed)
            break
            
        current_time = time.monotonic()
        if current_time >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(
                f"Timeout reached while waiting for port {port}. Max wait={max_wait}s"
            )
            
        time.sleep(0.25)

def port_is_listening(port: int, address: str = "127.0.0.1") -> bool:
    """Determine whether a port is currently in use/listening
    
    Args:
        port (int): Port number to check
        address (str): Host address to test against (default: '127.0.0.1')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if port is in use, False otherwise
    """
    with managed_socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as test_socket:
        try:
            test_socket.bind((address, port))
            # If bind succeeds, port is free
            return False
        except OSError as error:
            # EADDRINUSE means port is already in use
            if error.errno == errno.EADDRINUSE:
                return True
            # Re-raise unexpected errors
            raise

def find_free_port() -> int:
    """Acquire a currently unused port number from the OS
    
    Note: This doesn't guarantee the port will remain free after returning.
    
    Returns:
        int: A free port number assigned by the OS
    """
    with managed_socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) as temp_socket:
        temp_socket.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
        _, port = temp_socket.getsockname()[:2]
        return port

# Click CLI configuration
HELP_OPTIONS = dict(help_option_names=["-h", "--help"])

@click.group(context_settings=HELP_OPTIONS)
def main():
    """Utility commands for network port management"""

@main.command(name="wait")
@click.argument("port", type=click.IntRange(0, 65535))
@click.argument("timeout", type=click.FloatRange(0.0, 300.0))
@click.option("--quiet", is_flag=True, help="Suppress output messages")
@click.pass_context
def main_wait(ctx: click.Context, port, timeout, quiet):
    """
    Wait for a TCP port to become available
    
    \b
    PORT     Port number to monitor
    TIMEOUT  Maximum time to wait in seconds (max 300)
    
    \b
    Example: Wait up to 45 seconds for port 8080
        python3 -m c8ylp.helper wait 8080 45
    """

    except TimeoutError:
        if not quiet:
            click.secho(f"Port {port} did not open within {timeout} seconds", fg="red")
        ctx.exit(1)

def main_port():
    """
    Request a temporary free port number from the operating system
    
    \b
    Example: Get a random available port
        python3 -m c8ylp.helper port
    """
    click.echo(find_free_port())

import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import random
from itertools import product
from joblib import Parallel, delayed
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib import rcParams
rcParams["figure.autolayout"] = True

# Progressive learning imports (same as original)
from proglearn.progressive_learner import ProgressiveLearner
from proglearn.deciders import SimpleArgmaxAverage
from proglearn.transformers import TreeClassificationTransformer
from proglearn.voters import TreeClassificationVoter

def partition_data(
    features, labels, samples_per_task, num_tasks=10, task_offset=1, fold_index=0, current_task=0
):
    # Use stratified k-fold cross-validation to split data
    cv_splitter = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=6, shuffle=True, random_state=fold_index + 42)
    for _ in range(task_offset):
        train_indices, test_indices = next(cv_splitter.split(features, labels))
    
    X_train_fold, y_train_fold = features[train_indices], labels[train_indices]
    X_test_fold, y_test_fold = features[test_indices], labels[test_indices]
    
    # Randomly select classes for this configuration
    class_pool = np.arange(100)
    chosen_classes = np.random.choice(class_pool, size=num_tasks, replace=False)
    
    # Collect indices per class in training set
    class_train_indices = [np.where(y_train_fold == c)[0] for c in chosen_classes]
    
    # Compute how many samples per class per slot
    samples_per_class_per_slot = [
        len(indices) // num_tasks for indices in class_train_indices
    ]
    
    # Sample points from each class
    sampled_indices = []
    for idx, class_idx in enumerate(chosen_classes):
        available = class_train_indices[idx]
        n_samples = min(samples_per_class_per_slot[idx], len(available))
        sampled_indices.extend(np.random.choice(available, size=n_samples, replace=False))
    
    # Final sample selection for current task
    final_train_indices = np.random.choice(sampled_indices, size=samples_per_task, replace=False)
    X_train_task = X_train_fold[final_train_indices]
    y_train_task = y_train_fold[final_train_indices]
    
    # Prepare test set for chosen classes
    test_mask = np.isin(y_test_fold, chosen_classes)
    X_test_task = X_test_fold[test_mask]
    y_test_task = y_test_fold[test_mask]
    
    return X_train_task, y_train_task, X_test_task, y_test_task

def lifelong_training_experiment(
    X_data, y_data, forest_size, offset, fold_id, samples_per_task, num_tasks, seed=None
):
    results_df = pd.DataFrame(columns=["data_fold", "slot", "accuracy"])
    
    # Initialize random state if provided
    if seed is not None:
        np.random.seed(seed)
    
    # First task setup
    X_t0, y_t0, X_test_t0, y_test_t0 = partition_data(
        X_data, y_data, samples_per_task, num_tasks=num_tasks, 
        task_offset=offset, fold_index=fold_id
    )
    
    # Build progressive learner with uncertainty forest components
    pl_model = ProgressiveLearner(
        default_transformer_class=TreeClassificationTransformer,
        default_transformer_kwargs={"kwargs": {"max_depth": 30}},
        default_voter_class=TreeClassificationVoter,
        default_voter_kwargs={},
        default_decider_class=SimpleArgmaxAverage,
    )
    
    # Train first task
    pl_model.add_task(
        X=X_t0,
        y=y_t0,
        num_transformers=forest_size,
        transformer_voter_decider_split=[0.67, 0.33, 0.0],
        decider_kwargs={"classes": np.unique(y_t0)},
    )
    
    # Evaluate initial task
    pred_t0 = pl_model.predict(X_test_t0, task_id=0)
    acc_t0 = np.mean(pred_t0 == y_test_t0)
    
    # Record baseline performance
    results_df = results_df.append({
        "data_fold": offset,
        "slot": fold_id,
        "accuracy": acc_t0
    }, ignore_index=True)
    
    # Continue adding tasks
    for t_idx in range(1, num_tasks):
        # Get new task data
        X_new, y_new, _, _ = partition_data(
            X_data, y_data, samples_per_task, num_tasks=num_tasks,
            task_offset=offset, fold_index=fold_id, current_task=t_idx
        )
        
        # Add transformer for new task
        pl_model.add_transformer(
            X=X_new,
            y=y_new,
            transformer_data_proportion=1.0,
            num_transformers=forest_size,
            backward_task_ids=[0],
        )
        
 # Re-evaluate task 0 after each new task
        pred_t0 = pl_model.predict(X_test_t0, task_id=0)
        acc_t0 = np.mean(pred_t0 == y_test_t0)
        
        # Append result
        results_df = results_df.append({
            "data_fold": offset,
            "slot": fold_id,
            "accuracy": acc_t0
        }, ignore_index=True)
    
    return results_df

def run_batch_experiments(
    X_full, y_full, n_trees, samples_per_task, total_tasks, slot=0, shift=1
):
    return lifelong_training_experiment(
        X_full, y_full, n_trees, shift, slot, samples_per_task, total_tasks, seed=12345
    )

def compute_bte_metrics(df_collection, num_slots, num_shifts):
    bte_values = []
    
    for s in range(num_slots):
        for sh in range(num_shifts):
            df = df_collection[sh * num_slots + s]
            
            # Compute error rates
            errors = 1 - df["accuracy"]
            
            # BTE = error_initial / error_current
            bte_series = errors.iloc[0] / errors
            
            bte_values.append(bte_series.values)
    
    return bte_values

def visualize_bte(bte_data, font_size=14, tick_font=12):
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
    
    # Clean up plot appearance
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.yaxis.set_ticks_position("left")
    ax.xaxis.set_ticks_position("bottom")
    
    # Plot BTE curve
    ax.plot(
        range(len(bte_data)),
        bte_data,
        color="darkred",
        linewidth=2.5,
        linestyle="-",
        label="Lifelong Forest"
    )
    
    ax.set_xlabel("Tasks Seen", fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_ylabel("BTE (Task 1)", fontsize=font_size)
    ax.set_yticks([1.0, 1.1, 1.2])
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=tick_font)
    ax.legend(fontsize=font_size)
    
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

    help="Process PCAP data from stdin, apply user-defined filter function, output to stdout. "
         "Example: tcpdump -i INTERFACE -s0 -w - | pcapfilter -m myfilter.py | wireshark -k -i -",
    epilog="Standard input/output handle PCAP data; logs go to stderr.",
)
@click.option(
    "-m",
    "--module-name",
    type=str,
    default="",
    help="Python module containing packet_filter(packet) function. Can be generated via -w."
)
@click.option("-q", "--quiet", is_flag=True, help="Suppress log messages on STDERR")
@click.option("-o", "--legacy-pcap", is_flag=True, help="Use legacy Pcap format for input")
@click.option("-u", "--auto-reload", is_flag=True, help="Auto-reload module when source changes")
@click.option("-t", "--generate-template", type=str, help="Generate sample filter file")
@click.option(
    "-x", "--docker-guide", is_flag=True, help="Show Docker-specific help"
)
def main(module_name, quiet, legacy_pcap, auto_reload, generate_template, docker_guide):
    # Setup logging early
    setup_logging(not quiet)
    logger.debug("Starting application")
    
    # Handle Docker help case first
    if docker_guide:
        show_docker_assistance()
        return
    
    # Template generation logic
    if generate_template:
        if auto_reload:
            logger.warning("Module reloading cannot be enabled during template creation")
            return
        if module_name:
            logger.warning("Module name should follow -t flag, not precede it")
        if os.path.exists(generate_template):
            logger.critical("File '%s' already exists - will not overwrite", generate_template)
            return 4
        
        logger.info("Generating template file: %s", generate_template)
        with open(generate_template, "w") as fp:
            fp.write(FILTER_TEMPLATE)
        return 0
    
    # Choose reader based on format preference
    try:
        if not legacy_pcap:
            logger.info("Using PcapNg format reader")
            from scapy.all import PcapNgReader as Reader
        else:
            logger.info("Using legacy Pcap format reader")
            from scapy.all import PcapReader as Reader
    except ImportError as e:
        logger.error("Failed to import Scapy readers: %s", str(e))
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Import writer and core filter logic
    try:
        from scapy.all import PcapWriter as Writer
        from .pcapfilter import run_filter
    except ImportError as e:
        logger.error("Failed to import Scapy components: %s", str(e))
        sys.exit(1)
    
    # Execute filtering pipeline
    run_filter(
        _input=sys.stdin,
        _output=sys.stdout,
        reader_class=Reader,
        writer_class=Writer,
        module=module_name,
        reload=auto_reload,
    )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())  # pragma: no cover

from flask import Blueprint, render_template, request, redirect, url_for, flash
from flask_login import login_user
from sqlalchemy.exc import StatementError

# Define the login blueprint with URL prefix
login_bp = Blueprint('login', __name__, url_prefix="/login")

# Import models and forms
from ..models.user import User
from ..models.token import Token
from .forms import LoginForm
from .events import *

@login_bp.route('/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def index():
    # Extract token and name from query parameters for GET requests
    token_param = request.args.get("token", None) if request.method == 'GET' else ""
    name_param = request.args.get("name", None) if request.method == 'GET' else None
    
    form = LoginForm()
    
    # Process form submission
    if form.validate_on_submit():
        name_param = form.name.data
        token_param = form.token.data.strip() if form.token.data else None
    
    # Attempt to authenticate using provided credentials
    if name_param and token_param:
        try:
            token_record = Token.query.get(token_param)
        except StatementError:
            token_record = None
        
        if token_record and token_record.is_valid():
            user = token_record.user
            
            # Create new user if token is not associated with any user yet
            if user is None:
                user = User(name=name_param, token=token_record)
                db.session.add(user)
            
            db.session.commit()
            login_user(user)
            return redirect(request.args.get('next') or url_for("chat.index"))
        
        # Flash error message for invalid token
        flash("The token is either expired, was already used, or isn't correct at all.", "error")
    
    # Pre-fill form with existing values
    form.token.data = token_param
    form.name.data = name_param
    
    return render_template('login.html', form=form, title="slurk - Login")

from onapsdk.configuration import settings
from onapsdk.onap_service import OnapService as Onap
from onapsdk.sdc.service import Service
from onapsdk.exceptions import ResourceNotFound
from onapsdk.utils.headers_creator import headers_clamp_creator


class Clamp(Onap):
    """Mother Class of all CLAMP elements."""
    
    _base_url = settings.CLAMP_URL
    name: str = "CLAMP"
    headers = headers_clamp_creator(Onap.headers)
    
    @classmethod
    def base_url(cls) -> str:
        """Return the base URL for CLAMP API v2 endpoints."""
        return f"{cls._base_url}/restservices/clds/v2"
    
    @classmethod
    def find_loop_template(cls, service: Service) -> str:
        """
        Find and return loop template name if it exists for the given service.
        
        Args:
            service (Service): The distributed SDC service with TCA blueprint artifact
            
        Raises:
            ResourceNotFound: If no matching template is found
            
        Returns:
            str: The name of the matching template
        """
        url = f"{cls.base_url()}/templates/"
        templates = cls.send_message_json('GET', 'Get Loop Templates', url)
        
        # Use list comprehension to find matching templates
        matching_templates = [
            template["name"] 
            for template in templates 
            if template["modelService"]["serviceDetails"]["name"] == service.name
        ]
        
        if not matching_templates:
            raise ResourceNotFound("Template not found.")
            
        return matching_templates[0]
    
    @classmethod
    def verify_policy_existence(cls, policy_name: str, min_policies: int = 30) -> bool:
        """
        Verify that a specific policy exists in CLAMP and sufficient policies are present.
        
        Args:
            policy_name (str): Policy acronym to check
            min_policies (int): Minimum required number of policies in CLAMP
            
        Returns:
            bool: True if policy exists and minimum policy count is met
        """
        url = f"{cls.base_url()}/policyToscaModels/"
        policies = cls.send_message_json('GET', 'Get stocked policies', url)
        
        # Check if any policy matches using next() with generator expression
        policy_found = any(
            policy["policyAcronym"] == policy_name 
            for policy in policies
        )
        
        # Return True only if both conditions are satisfied
        return len(policies) >= min_policies and policy_found

# Training script for image classification using PyTorch
# This module handles argument parsing, model loading, data preparation,
# and training loop execution

import argparse
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

from classification.data_loader import get_loaders
from classification.model_loader import get_model
from classification.trainer import Trainer


def parse_arguments():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Image Classification Training Pipeline")
    
    # Required arguments
    parser.add_argument("--model_path", required=True, help="Path to save/load the trained model")
    
    # Device configuration
    parser.add_argument("--device_id", type=int, default=0 if torch.cuda.is_available() else -1)
    
    # Data split ratios
    parser.add_argument("--train_split", type=float, default=0.6)
    parser.add_argument("--val_split", type=float, default=0.2)
    parser.add_argument("--test_split", type=float, default=0.2)
    
    # Training hyperparameters
    parser.add_argument("--batch_size", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--max_epochs", type=int, default=20)
    parser.add_argument("--verbosity", type=int, default=2)
    
    # Model and dataset specifications
    parser.add_argument("--architecture", type=str, default="resnet")
    parser.add_argument("--data_name", type=str, default="catdog")
    parser.add_argument("--num_classes", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--freeze_layers", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--load_pretrained", action="store_true")
    
    args = parser.parse_args()
    return args


def run_training_pipeline(config):
    # Set up computation device
    device = (
        torch.device("cpu")
        if config.device_id < 0
        else torch.device(f"cuda:{config.device_id}")
    )
    
    # Initialize model and move to device
    model, input_dim = get_model(config)
    model = model.to(device)
    
    # Prepare data loaders
    train_loader, val_loader, test_loader = get_loaders(config, input_dim)
    print("Training samples:", len(train_loader.dataset))
    print("Validation samples:", len(val_loader.dataset))
    print("Test samples:", len(test_loader.dataset))
    
    # Configure optimizer and loss function
    optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters())
    loss_fn = nn.NLLLoss()
    
    # Display configuration details if verbosity is high enough
    if config.verbosity >= 2:
        print(model)
        print(optimizer)
        print(loss_fn)
    
    # Initialize trainer and start training
    trainer = Trainer(config)
    trainer.fit(model, loss_fn, optimizer, train_loader, val_loader)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    config = parse_arguments()
    run_training_pipeline(config)

# CoverArt implementation with caching and image processing

from collections import OrderedDict
from io import BytesIO
import os
from PIL import Image  # type: ignore
import re
import sys
from typing import Optional, Iterable, List
from config import config

class CoverNotFoundError(FileNotFoundError):
    pass

class CoverArt:
    """
    >>> cover = CoverArt(
    ...     "/path/to/artist/album/song.flac",
    ...     hints=["The Beatles", "White Album"]
    ... )
    >>> cover.get()
    "/path/to/artist/album/cover.jpg"
    >>> cover.get_data()
    b'\x01\x02...'
    """
    standard_names: List[str] = ["cover", "folder"]
    extensions: List[str] = ["png", "jpeg", "jpg", "bmp", "gif"]
    _cache: OrderedDict = OrderedDict()
    _cache_capacity = config.cover_scan_cache_size
    
    def __new__(
        cls, audio_dir: str, audio_relpath: str, hints: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None
    ):
        """A caching constructor for cover images for audio files.
        Searches for matching image files around the given audio file and selects one or
        none. Transparently returns a previous instance if the image path was already
        seen for another audio file. Images are evicted from the cache after
        a number (set in config.cover_scan_cache_size) of other images have been loaded.
        """
        audio_path = os.path.join(audio_dir, audio_relpath)
        
        # Normalize hints to lowercase
        normalized_hints = []
        if hints:
            for hint in hints:
                normalized_hints.append(hint.lower())
        
        image_abspath = cls._search(audio_path, normalized_hints)
        if image_abspath is None:
            raise CoverNotFoundError(f"No cover art for {audio_path!r}")
        
        image_path = os.path.relpath(image_abspath, audio_dir)
        
        # Cache management
        if image_path not in cls._cache:
            instance = super().__new__(cls)
            cls._cache[image_path] = instance
            instance.image_path = image_path
        else:
            # Move to end for LRU behavior
            cls._cache.move_to_end(image_path)
            
        # Enforce cache size limit
        if len(cls._cache) > config.cover_scan_cache_size:
            oldest_key = next(iter(cls._cache))
            del cls._cache[oldest_key]
            
        return cls._cache[image_path]
    
    def __init__(self, audio_dir: str, *args):
        self.audio_dir = audio_dir
        self.image_mtime: Optional[int] = None
        self.image_data: Optional[BytesIO] = None
        self.image_path: str  # set in __new__, declared here for typing
        
    @classmethod
    def _search(cls, audio_path: str, hints: Iterable[str]) -> Optional[str]:
        """Search for coverart files and return the best candidate.
        Searches dir containing the file and, if no images were found among sibling
        files, the parent directory too.
        """
        file_dir = os.path.dirname(audio_path)
        parent_dir = os.path.dirname(file_dir)
        candidates = []
        max_filesize: Optional[int] = None
        
        search_dirs = [file_dir, parent_dir]
        for directory in search_dirs:
            try:
                files_in_dir = os.listdir(directory)
            except OSError:
                continue
                
            for filename in files_in_dir:
                filename_lower = filename.lower()
                
                # Check if file has valid image extension
                has_valid_extension = False
                for ext in cls.extensions:
                    if filename_lower.endswith(ext):
                        has_valid_extension = True
                        break
                        
                if not has_valid_extension:
                    continue
                    
                filepath = os.path.join(directory, filename)
                try:
                    filesize = os.stat(filepath).st_size
                except OSError:
                    continue
                    
                candidates.append((filepath, filename_lower, filesize))
                
                # Track maximum file size
                if max_filesize is None or filesize > max_filesize:
                    max_filesize = filesize
                    
            # Stop searching if we found candidates in current directory
            if candidates:
                break
                
        # Score and sort candidates if any exist
        if candidates and max_filesize:
            def score_candidate(candidate):
                return cls._rate_as_cover_file(
                    candidate[1], hints, candidate[2], max_filesize
                )
                
            candidates.sort(key=score_candidate, reverse=True)
            return candidates[0][0]
            
        return None
    
    @classmethod
    def _rate_as_cover_file(
        cls, filename_lower: str, hints: Iterable[str], filesize: int, max_filesize: int
    ) -> float:
        rating = 0.0
        
        # Check for standard cover names
        for name in cls.standard_names:
            if name in filename_lower:
                rating += 0.6
                break
                
        # Check for hint matches
        for hint in hints:
            if hint in filename_lower:
                rating += 0.3
                break
                
        # File size contribution
        rating += (filesize / max_filesize) * 0.5
        
        ### Checking for image size is quite expensive. Turn it off, and rely on
        ### filesize as a rough gauge for image quality.
        # img = Image.open(os.path.join(path, filename))
        # if any([s < config.cover_max_dimension for s in img.size]):
        #     rating *= 0.5
        return rating
    
    def get_data(self, image_format="JPEG") -> Optional[bytes]:
        """Load (and possibly resize to fit cover_max_dimension) the cover image.
        Returns the bytes of the image file in the given *image_format*, or None on
        error.
        """
        if self.image_data is not None:
            return self.image_data.getvalue()
            
        self.image_data = BytesIO()
        try:
            full_image_path = os.path.join(self.audio_dir, self.image_path)
            image = Image.open(full_image_path)
            
            # Resize if needed
            if any([s > config.cover_max_dimension for s in image.size]):
                scale = config.cover_max_dimension / max(image.size)
                new_size = (
                    int(image.size[0] * scale),
                    int(image.size[1] * scale)
                )
                image = image.resize(new_size, Image.LANCZOS)
                
            image.save(self.image_data, image_format)
        except OSError as err:
            error_msg = str(err)
            if "cannot write mode" in error_msg:
                # Convert image mode and retry
                image.convert("RGB").save(self.image_data, image_format)
            else:
                # Handle other image errors
                print(
                    f"Warning, image data load/save failed for {self.image_path}:",
                    err,
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
                return None
        return self.image_data.getvalue()
    
    def __hash__(self) -> int:
        return hash(self.image_path)
    
    def __eq__(self, other) -> bool:
        try:
            if self.image_path is None or other.image_path is None:
                return False
            return self.image_path == other.image_path
        except AttributeError:
            return False

# Type III Clone: PRGPlotter class with modified logic and structure
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional, List, Tuple
import numpy as np
from matplotlib import pyplot as plt
from clscurves.plotter.plotter import MetricsPlotter

class PRGPlotter(MetricsPlotter):
    """Visualize the Precision-Recall-Gain (PRG) curve.
    
    Implements plotting functionality for PRG curves as described in:
    'Precision-Recall-Gain' paper available at https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2015/file/33e8075e9970de0cfea955afd4644bb2-Paper.pdf
    
    Note: Weighted recall variants are not supported due to unclear theoretical interpretation.
    """
    
    def __init__(
            self,
            data_dict: Dict[str, Any],
            is_probabilistic: bool):
        # Renamed parameters and internal handling
        super().__init__(data_dict, is_probabilistic)
        
    def draw_prg_curve(
            self,
            plot_title: str = "Precision-Recall-Gain Curve",
            colormap: str = "rainbow",
            coloring_scheme: str = "thresh",
            color_limits: Optional[List[float]] = None,
            colorbar_title: str = None,
            resolution: int = None,
            with_bootstrap: bool = False,
            bootstrap_transparency: float = 0.15,
            bootstrap_line_color: str = "black",
            operating_point: Optional[float] = None,
            return_figure: bool = False) -> Optional[Tuple[plt.figure, plt.axes]]:
        """Generate a Precision-Recall-Gain curve visualization.
        
        Parameters
        ----------
        plot_title : str
            Title displayed on the generated plot.
        colormap : str
            Matplotlib colormap identifier for point coloring.
        coloring_scheme : str
            Determines basis for coloring points; either "frac" (fraction flagged)
            or "thresh" (score threshold).
        color_limits : Optional[List[float]]
            Custom range [min, max] for color scale if desired.
        colorbar_title : str
            Label for colorbar; defaults to scheme-appropriate text.
        resolution : int
            Output DPI setting; default uses matplotlib's standard.
        with_bootstrap : bool
            Whether to overlay bootstrapped curves for uncertainty estimation.
        bootstrap_transparency : float
            Opacity level for bootstrap curve rendering.
        bootstrap_line_color : str
            Color specification for bootstrap lines.
        operating_point : Optional[float]
            Threshold value for confidence ellipse annotation.
        return_figure : bool
            If True, returns figure and axes instead of displaying.
        """
        # Use alternative key names for retrieval
        x_data_key = "recall_gain"
        y_data_key = "precision_gain"
        x_vals = self.data_dict[x_data_key]
        y_vals = self.data_dict[y_data_key]
        
        # Generate visualization based on mode
        if not with_bootstrap:
            fig, ax = self._construct_plot(
                x_vals[:, 0], y_vals[:, 0], colormap, resolution, 
                coloring_scheme, color_limits, colorbar_title)
        else:
            fig, ax = self._construct_bootstrap_plot(
                x_vals, y_vals, colormap, resolution, 
                coloring_scheme, color_limits, colorbar_title,
                bootstrap_transparency, bootstrap_line_color)
        
        # Compute derived metrics
        prg_auc_val = self.data_dict["prg_auc"]
        prg_auc_mean = np.mean(prg_auc_val) if isinstance(prg_auc_val, np.ndarray) and with_bootstrap else prg_auc_val[0]
        
        imbalance_param = self.data_dict["imbalance"]
        imb_mean = np.mean(imbalance_param) if isinstance(imbalance_param, np.ndarray) and with_bootstrap else imbalance_param[0]
        
        # Calculate derived ratio metric
        class_ratio_val = 1 / (imb_mean + 1e-9) - 1
        
        # Draw baseline reference line
        ax.plot([0, 1], [1, 0], "k-", linewidth=1.2)
        
        # Annotate AUC value
        ax.text(
            x=0.06, y=0.13,
            s=f"{'Mean ' if with_bootstrap else ''}AUPRG = {prg_auc_mean:.3f}",
            ha="left", va="center",
            bbox=dict(facecolor="gray", alpha=0.1, boxstyle="round"))
        
        # Annotate class imbalance
        ax.text(
            x=0.06, y=0.07,
            s=f"{'Mean ' if with_bootstrap else ''}Class Imb. = {class_ratio_val:.1f} : 1",
            ha="left", va="center",
            bbox=dict(facecolor="gray", alpha=0.1, boxstyle="round"))
        
        # Add confidence ellipse if requested
        if operating_point is not None:
            self._insert_op_ellipse(
                op_value=operating_point,
                x_key=x_data_key,
                y_key=y_data_key,
                ax=ax,
                thresh_key=coloring_scheme)
        
        # Finalize axis labels and title
        ax.set_xlabel("Recall Gain = (Rec - pp)/((1 - pp) * Rec)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Precision Gain = (Prec - pp)/((1 - pp) * Prec)")
        ax.set_title(plot_title)
        
        # Handle output method
        if return_figure:
            return fig, ax
        else:
            plt.show()
            plt.close()
